marie: quick RFC follow-up 1 1 Need a minimal rollback playbook for customers cut over from shared peering to per-tenant ephemeral relays. Goals: preserve client src IP when possible, avoid lease exhaustion, fast 1-command rollback. Keep it short.

devops: short checklist: 1) page #ops & #networking, attach INC; 2) run preflight (snat + long sessions); 3) reduce canary to 0% if problems; 4) rollback command; 5) scale controllers if lease-exhaustion.

devops: exact commands (examples):
```bash
# preflight
opsctl customer preflight --customer=cust-900 --fields=snat,active_sessions --ticket=INC-2026-9000
# fast rollback -> single op
opsctl route rollback --customer=cust-900 --to=shared-peering --ticket=INC-2026-9000
# if leases exhausted -> increase reserved pool
curl -s -X POST https://ops.internal/egress/v1/leases -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN" -d '{"customer":"cust-900","count":20,"region":"us-west-2"}'
# scale controllers to relieve pressure
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/egress-operator --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy egress-operator -o jsonpath='{.status.availableReplicas}')+2))
```
own: metrics to watch: egress.lease_pool_available, relay.health, cp.request_latency, tcp.session_abort_rate. Rule: if lease_pool_available < 12% -> immediately reduce canary weight by 50% and alert oncall.

audit-bot: NOTE: every opsctl/curl must include --ticket or X-Audit-Ticket header; please append ticket to commands.

marie: perfect. I'll add this snippet to the RFC reply. Keep replies short. :thumbsup:
